- **Paper: "ChatGPT tells 20 versions of its prototypical story..." (Bill Benzon, Feb 2024)**
  - Benzon prompts ChatGPT with the single word "story" 20 times: 10 stories generated within one continuous session, 10 generated each in its own fresh session
  - Nearly all 20 stories share a prototypical shape: a curious young woman protagonist ventures from home into a magical/fairy-tale world, has an adventure, and returns to benefit her community
  - Protagonist name "Elara" recurs strikingly: 2/10 in the single-session set vs. 5/10 in the separate-session set, taken as rough evidence that a shared session context increases variety across outputs
  - Argues this prototypical story is an abstraction ChatGPT extracted from the mass of stories in its training corpus, and thus offers a clue to the model's underlying structure
  - Frames the project as an alternative/complement to mechanistic interpretability ("popping the hood"): using Pinker's olive-pitter analogy, argues you must study what a system is *for* (via systematic input/output probing) since inspecting internal parts alone won't reveal purpose
  - Explicitly rejects "stochastic parrot"/"autocomplete on steroids" framings, arguing the model has real structure worth reverse-engineering through behavioral experiments
  - Includes all 20 full generated stories as an appendix/dataset supporting the analysis

- **Student's sidenote (slide deck, "Version 2")**
  - Summarizes Benzon's setup, prototype pattern, and three central claims (single-vs-separate session variety, prototype-as-training-corpus-abstraction, blackbox-study value)
  - Defines an 8-element evaluation rubric to score stories against the prototype (Home, Departure, Magical World, Helpers, Challenge, Growth, Return, Community Benefit), each scored 0/0.5/1
  - **Experiment 1**: replicates Benzon's single-vs-separate-session design using Llama-3.1-8B; finds single-session stories more coherent (10/10) vs. separate-session (7/10, with 3 degenerating into incoherent text); shows a striking example of model output collapsing into gibberish under a bare "story" prompt with no session context
  - **Experiment 2**: varies the prompt itself ("story" vs. "Tell me a story" vs. "Write a story"); more explicit prompts eliminate the incoherence seen with the bare one-word prompt
  - **Experiment 3**: compares model scale/training (Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash) on the same prompt; larger/differently-trained models are more robust to the terse prompt, and DeepSeek produces a noticeably different "default story," suggesting the fairy-tale prototype is a property of training corpus rather than universal to all LLMs
  - Evaluates Benzon's three claims against these results: partially supports the session-variety claim but reinterprets it (single-session stories vary in surface details like names/settings but keep the same underlying storyline); supports the training-corpus-abstraction claim, using DeepSeek's divergent stories as evidence the prototype is corpus-specific, not universal; endorses the blackbox-study value claim, framing the prototype pattern as a diagnostic signal about a model's training data
  - Draws connections to Benzon's related working paper (protagonist traits shaping story adaptation) and to Ramesh/Dori's work on certifiable autonomous systems, casting both as blackbox/empirical performance-characterization approaches applied to opaque systems
